feature: A shape's bar never vanishes from its track, and an empty track can take one back
summary: Deleting, grouping or carrying away a shape no longer leaves an empty row behind, a bar can never be dragged shorter than a frame, and an empty track's right-click menu adds a rectangle or text to it, pastes onto it, or puts a stray layer on it.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open any recording and open the timeline.

try.do: Draw a rectangle on the recording with the rectangle tool.
Press Delete. The rectangle and its Rectangle row both go; press Cmd+Z and both come back.
Drag the rectangle bar's right end left, past its start. It stops at one frame and stays a bar you can grab.
Click the + under the track headers, choose Video Track, then drag the rectangle's bar up onto the new empty track. Its old row goes.
Add another video track and right-click it: choose Add Text.
Check that the words land on that track from the playhead.
Add one more track, right-click it and choose Delete Empty Tracks.

evaluate: Is it right that deleting a shape also removes the row the app made for it, while a track you added yourself stays until you delete it?
V1 and Audio stay when their recording is carried off or deleted, the way Premiere keeps them. Is that what you expect?
Is Add Rectangle / Add Text / Paste Here on an empty track's right-click menu where you would look for it?
Is a one frame bar, drawn at least 6 points wide, easy enough to grab back and stretch?
rough: Add Text lands a layer called Text and the title look runs from the playhead to the end of the shot, not five seconds; only Put on Timeline gives exactly five seconds.
The layers list cannot be dragged onto a track in Next: with the timeline open the timeline IS the layers list, so the two are never on screen together. A bar carried up or down is the drag.

Put on Timeline (canvas and layer right-click) and the empty track's Put Layer Here are covered by tests only: at Next defaults every shape drawn on a video already gets a bar, so a layer on no track only comes from older documents, and no walk can make one without turning a flag off.
Paste Here lands in the paste's own undo step but was not walked, because a walk's clipboard is the person's clipboard.
The mock (video.html, the timeline) draws no track right-click menu, so the rows follow Premiere's names: Delete Track, Delete Empty Tracks.
